text: EncodeDirect writes the escape byte followed by a hyphen, so it requires two destination bytes. With less space it returns the more-output status before writing or advancing that source character; the final consumed/written counts reflect the actual pointer advances. The ordinary direct branch still needs one byte. The modified UTF-7 subclass supplies ampersand as escape. This proves the local buffer/count contract, not the whole converter or crash cure. The separate wrapper checks belong to the following patch, and no boundary test or native execution ran.
title: The UTF-7 escape branch reserves two bytes before consuming the character
